label: EXPERIMENTAL snowpack-structure prediction for expert decision support. Not an avalanche forecast, danger rating or operational guidance.
source: Avalanche Canada Mountain Information Network (public reports)

reports.title: Sunshine Slack
reports.comment: quick: Skied Quartz ridge nw face , Laryx glades and rock isle and Stuck to mellow slopes. Alpine was wind scoured or hard (pencil) wild slab supportive to skis and unreactive in the morning. Snow pack ranged from 5-50. Treeline down to the lakes we’re great skiing seeing 40-100 Cms of fist on 4f In sheltered lees. Snowpack ranged from 60-200 cms. TO NOTE: rapid solar effect to S/SW slopes were no…

reports.title: Grizzley Glades
reports.comment: quick: Skied untouched sheltered burned trees on a SE aspect through Grizzley Glades above Grizzly Lake. Skinning in through the bottom of Twin Cairns in tree-line/sub alpine. Noticeable wind skin on E aspects, on average 2cm thick. No noticeable wind effect skiing down through the burned trees. Made for some nice turns on fist to 4F snow. Worth noting Surface Hoar averaging 3mm up to 5mm througho…

reports.title: Bourgeau Left
reports.comment: quick: Bailed off of Bourgeau Left today due to rapid melting and rock fall.  Wall is in the sun by 10am, and was shedding almost immediately after.  First 2 pitches climbed well with good sticks and screws throughout. Upper pitches also looked great! Very intense sun trap in there and despite the cold temps it felt way too warm on the wall.

reports.title: Bourgeau Right ice climb
reports.comment: quick: We climbed Bourgeau Right today, ice conditions were amazing. Mostly freshly reformed, dense, almost plastic ice, great screws, secure placements. Most of the horrible eggshell encountered on all the other climbs this early season is gone. A few shallow spots on topouts and between pitches. All the bolted anchors are dug out and dry. Last pitch was quite sun affected, but still manageable a…

reports.title: Healy Main Drain
reports.comment: quick: Rode N face of Twin Cairns and then skinned over to Wawa Ridge and skied down to Healy Main Drain and out the summer hiking trail. Ridgetop was very thin and wind affected with tough travel on Twin Cairns, although the N face skied well. Open slopes had a thin windskin above 10-20cm of supportive pow, snow turned blower and got deeper on sheltered aspects. HS was around 50-70 on average. He…

reports.title: Bourgeau Right
reports.comment: quick: Warm and sunny day on Bourgeau Right, we topped out and began descending at 12:00. Things deteriorated very rapidly, culminating with a section of ice collapsing at 1pm just as we were doing our final rappel. The first 3 pitches of climbing were swept by the collapse and some small sections of ice collapsed in the following 15 minutes. Definitely a hot day to be up there, and wouldn't have …

reports.title: Sunshine Backcountry + Bourgeau Left
reports.comment:
quick: Bourgeau Left fell off sometime today.  Normal for this time of year.  

The alpine was windless and warm in the sun.  Which broke down the surface hoar on due south aspects.  The thin snow pack, cold nights have faceted out the snowpack which was worse on East and North aspects.   Found good skiing at treeline and below  on meadowy solar aspects.  Skiing on the polar aspects was fun but fe…

reports.title: Borgeau Left
reports.comment: quick: Observed from the SSV gondola this morning, Borgeau Left is gone for now. Couldn't see any debris on the ground below or above but it was dark. Didn't get eyes on Borgeau Right.

reports.title: Bear Spirit November 16, 2022
reports.comment:
quick: 2cm new snow, low wind down low, less than 15cm of snow on the ground and not much in the slopes and cliff bands above on approach. 

Ice conditions decent on the right side WI3 Bear Spirit flows, with a thin top out. Ice conditions poor on left WI4 flow, pillar not even touching down fully yet. Ice conditions on approach step to main flow areas were thin. River crossings on approach was pr…

reports.title: Bear Spirit November 16, 2022
reports.comment: quick: Ice climbed moderate right flows of Bear Spirit that are in. Left flow is not dropping down yet and not in. Not much snow on slopes above approach route, slopes of concern seemed below threshold.

reports.title: Healy Pass
reports.comment: quick: Trail is in good condition. A little faster and bumpier than usual. Hit one rock on the last downhill, lock the heels in for the steeper downs.  Near the pass mellow slopes at tree line in the sun skied well. Found some suncrust on steep SW aspects at treeline. No wind, another nice inversion.

reports.title: Healy pass
reports.comment: quick: Summer trail up to the pass is in great condition, highly recommended for getting the legs out for a stretch. Alpine coverage is poor but sheltered low angle slopes have good enough coverage for some safe turns. Wind affect is faceting out but still supportive enough for skiing. Lots of tracks but no MIN's. Seems the ice climbing community is outshining the skiers with sharing information. …

reports.title: Overcast Bourgeau Right
reports.comment: quick: Saved Bourgeau Right for a day with clouds forecast, was nice not to have to race to beat the reported failing and falling ice.

reports.title: Simpson Pass to Sunshine Ski Area
reports.comment: quick: Skied up Healy Creek to the bridge above the Campsite then headed up to Simpson Pass. Then over towards Twin Cairns (passed to the East of Twin Cairns) then across to the top of the Wawa chair. Took the Sunshine ski out. Best travel was staying in the trees and on tracks where possible. 8 cm of storm snow covered 30 cm of faceted sno so easy to sink through to rocks below surface. 30km wind…

reports.title: Mt Bourgeau
reports.comment:
quick: Skied up the track, and then skied down again. Got some turns on the track. We need more snow. Lol.
It was great to get out and get off the couch.

reports.title: Twin Cairns
reports.comment:
quick: Wandered up to the mellow south slopes on Twin Cairns - stayed away from steep alpine slopes due to slab concern. 

Recent wind (off W today) scattered new snow fall with lots of variability around ridge line. Where deep enough (80+cm), new snow seemed well bonded but we did not investigate much. 

A few decent turns, but many sharks still lurk just beneath the new snow. Not worth it unless…

reports.title: Too much snow
reports.comment: quick: Summer trail for Healy Pass had very good coverage with 5-10cm of fresh snow. Coming out of the trees in the open larch slopes there was 15-30cm. Too much snow for those low angles!  Could feel some wind slabs in the open areas.

reports.title: Rock Isle Lake
reports.comment: quick: Went for a walk to Rock Isle lake from top of standish. On southern aspects, the crust is still breakable under 20cm new snow. Good snow on NE aspects, but still punches down to rock, and starting to get pretty tracked out. Recent avalanche on an eastern aspect next to the lake, estimate 30m wide, sz 1. / snowpack: Dug on an eastern aspect. HS 65-82cm. Found 20cm of PP fist snow sits on top…

reports.title: PC Sunshine Study Plot
reports.comment: snowpack: See Attached Profile

reports.title: SSV slack / Twin Cairns
reports.comment: quick: Toured SSV slack including Grizzly trees and Twin Cairns traverse and N descent. Quite a few settlements observed with cracking over the entire day but since we were fairly low angle nothing moved. No significant obs to report otherwise - ski pen of about 40cm. Facets galore on the ridge traverse of twin cairns which was extra bony. Skied down the N run and wind skin (5cm) did go but no ent…

reports.title: Spooky Snow
reports.comment: quick: Traversing the east side of Standish backcountry on our way over towards Grizzly. The snow is soft and not particularly supportive on this lee side. Everything windward (West facing) is completely wind scoured in the alpine. We were traversing south on relatively benign, rolling terrain (i.e. nothing steep) to get a feel of the snow. We were traveling on a bench with rolling convex slopes a…

reports.title: Backside of Bye-Bye Bowl
reports.comment: avalanche: Persistent slab triggered by a skier at a thin spot on rocks propagated 15m above the skier into deeper snowpack and released on a convex roll. The slab was running on facets.  No signs of instability noted before the incident. / incident: Avalanche was triggered by 3rd skier in the group which was taken down about 20m and ended up being partially buried but not injured. 1st skier was a…

reports.title: Healy Paths
reports.comment:
quick: Skier (skinner?) accidental size 1.5.
Snowpack was 30cm storm slab increasing from fist to finger hardness on top of a 5cm sun crust above facets to ground. 
Slab avalanche fractured about 10m above second person on uptrack on the sun crust/facet interface ~35cms down. 
Noticed whumpfing earlier on lower-angled slopes where the snowpack consisted of only the 30cm storm slab above facets to …

reports.title: Healy Pass
reports.comment: quick: Skier triggered size 2 and another skier remote triggered another size 2. Both on steeper, thinner more convex rocky terrain, not surprising to see.

reports.title: Wawa Bowl
reports.comment: quick: Great riding on mellower slopes around the practice slopes and Wawa Bowl. We didn't observe any whumpfing or notable cracking though I know others nearby on Twin Cairns did. Dug a pit in the practice slopes area. As expected, over 40 cms of new storm snow from the last week on top of a 10cm hard crust layer, with over 30cms of facets underneath.

reports.title: Simpson Pass
reports.comment: quick: While setting the up track many whumphs , and remote triggers were witnessed.  Early afternoon, a number of convex slopes above gulleys were sliding naturally. Our ski party chose to maintain elevation setting an easy efficient tracks without going into gullies and avalanche terrain, while others oddly did not, and moved slowly up these gulleys.

reports.title: Helay Pass
reports.comment: avalanche: Size 2 skier triggered (may have been remote trigger, I saw it happen from pretty far away hard to know) 80cm crown, slid on 2.5mm facits. CT Sudden collapse at L12, triggered on a thin spot that also happened to be convex. Loud wumphing all day, lots of evidence of natural Avis size ~1.5-2 on similar slopes.

reports.title: Rock isle
reports.comment: quick: Little poke around in the afternoon behind Standish chair and Rock isle lake. Found good riding with very little wind effect on the new snow. A couple big whumps on our way down to the lake. Average of 75-95cm HS. Good turns above the lake but starting to get tracked out. Dug a quick pit on our way back to the resort. Found a slightly stiffer layer down 18cm (4F) and then back to facets (F,…

reports.title: Healy main drain
reports.comment: quick: Skied Healy main drain today. Saw this 1.5 on our way into the drainage on a steep NE facing rocky shallow slope, looked a day or 2 old. We saw another older size 1 on a very similar feature. We walked and skied over a number of small wind loaded convexities on our way to the line and got little to no results. Not much wind effect in the area and windslabs even on steep convex roles where s…

reports.title: Simpson Pass
reports.comment: quick: Ski tour up Healy Creek to Sunshine Village with a snow profile at 2300m at Simpson Pass. The snowpack is 80 cm and very weak. Several very large whumphs were noted in open glades at 2100m. Foot penetration is to the ground, so you cannot walk around. Felt the need to avoid skiing any steep terrain that could produce an avalanche.

reports.title: Twin Cairns, Sa size 1
reports.comment: quick: Observed a small skier triggered slab from the lifts on the east aspect of twin cairns. See photo.  Unknown time and date.  Looked like it stepped down into the facets.

reports.title: Wawa Ridge
reports.comment: quick: Great day out on Wawa Ridge, thin snowpack on the wind-blasted alpine slopes (as expected), but the bowl near the summit skied well. Sunnier and less wind than forecasted! Zero instabilities noted all day, no whumphing or shooting cracks and we were carefully watching for these signs because of last week's min reports. Good fun powder on the bowl near the ridge summit, with deteriorating sn…

reports.title: Bourgeau Left - Natural avalanche activity
reports.comment:
avalanche: Several natural wind slab avalanches, size 1.5-2.5, occurred in the past 12+ hrs above the Bourgeau Left ice climb with at least one of them running over the climb. A couple of the wind slabs stepped down into the basal facets. 

Several other natural avalanches up to size 2 were also observed on Mt Bourgeau and above the Healy Creek trail triggered by the new snow and wind on Christmas…

reports.title: Booterville
reports.comment: quick: Walked up a mellow rib towards the south ridge of Twin cairns, stopped and dug a pit at the top of tree line below a small roll-over in the immediate lee. When approaching pit location(within 30m) I heard several large whumps isolated to that area. No cracking. I skied down the same way and slashed some small test slopes but nothing moved. / avalanche: Natural size 1.5 on Bourgeau above the…

reports.title: Bourgeau Right Natural Avalanche
reports.comment: avalanche: Sunshine staff reported seeing a size 2.5 natural avalanche run over the Bourgeau Right ice climb late in the day today. They were unable to see the start zone or debris due to failing light conditions, but it nearly dusted the parking lot.

reports.title: Sunshine Road avalanche control results
reports.comment: avalanche: Good results from helicopter bombing on the Sunshine village access road. Several paths produced wide propagations (up to 150 m) that ran on the crust/facet combo near the ground. Results in Eagle 3, Bourgeau 7 and Bourgeau 4.

reports.title: Grizzly Glades
reports.comment:
quick: Well preserved faceted snow in this area.
Sunk down to waist when you stepped off your board. 

No signs of instabilities on this slope. Rode like deep soft powder. 

Snow near wawa ridge had a denser damp top layer and was not as well preserved.

reports.title: Healy Pass- avalanches heard, not seen
reports.comment:
quick: Toured up to Healy Pass. Heard several large avalanches coming from the Egypt Lake area, couldn't see them due to poor visibility. 

Fresh, boot top powder on top of a fragile crust with facets underneath.

reports.title: Sunshine Meadows
reports.comment:
snowpack: CTM 13, 35 cm from surface, 1 mm facets / CTH 21, 75 cm from surface, 2 mm facets.

Having toured a few days this week, including Hwy93, mixed results in CT count... don't be fooled by a one-off stable CT.  93S area in trees test slopes popped on Dec. 17th facets and skin track kick-turns collapsing (limited propagation due to dense trees and deadfall).

reports.title: Healy pass Simpson pass Wawa ridge
reports.comment: quick: HS 100 cm at 2100m. Supportive layer down 30cm made for surprisingly OK travel and turns. We avoided avi terrain. PS 20 PF 100. Up to 5mm SH widespread at TL and BTL. Wx no wind -5celcius mid afternoon and sunny.. no recent avalanche activity observed.

reports.title: Healy pass/ridge walk
reports.comment: quick: Long slog up Healy pass trail today. We skied the trees off of Healy ridge. Conditions were good for skiing with boot top powder on top of a firmer layer. Surface hoar is forming in many locations. We did not hear any whumpfs but lots of crowns visible on the thin/rocky alpine slopes in the area

reports.title: Healy Pass area
reports.comment: quick: 25 cm of snow ontop a firmer layer; unconsolidated facets beneath that. Surface hoar found in the trees and protected areas. Increased winds on ridgetop. Found some good mellow skiing on West aspects and wind sheltered areas.

reports.title: Rock Isle Glades
reports.comment: quick: Cloudy day out, skinned up Sunshine then did a few short laps of low angle open trees above Rock Isle lake. Skiied well, about 5-10cm unconsolidated snow over a surprisingly supportive midpack. Dug a quick pit, HS 95cm (5-10cm surface snow over supportive 1F mid pack, 20cm of depth hoar at the bottom). Lots of whumpfing when breaking trail today, glad we were on mellow slopes. / snowpack: C…

reports.title: Grizzly Glades
reports.comment: quick: Skiied in the Sunshine Meadows at the Grizzly Glades to keep it safe. Did a couple of mellow runs in the Forrest before heading home as it started to get cloudy/windy. Stayed on 25~ degree slopes and under in the trees. No settlements observed but a few hastey pits showed ~1cm surface hoar down 10~ cm above the dense mid pack on sheltered slopes. In the larch forest the mid pack was less de…

reports.title: White wizard
reports.comment: quick: Toured up Wawa ridge and then dug a pit and skied the white wizard drainage out to Healy creek. Found surface hoar up to 2350m (highest we got.) Dug a pit in the meadow above the Healy drainages at 2200m (NW aspect) HS:108. Found up to 6mm depth hoar at the base and then mostly facets expect for the slab above the PWL which was 1F mostly rounds. Got a CTH23 (SC) for the PWL and CTH25 (SC) f…

reports.title: Wawa Ridge Bowl
reports.comment: quick: Chill tour along wawa ridge. No instabilities to report. a nice layer of snow on top of some hard base. Skied not too bad all considered. Heavily tracked!

reports.title: Monarch Ramparts East
reports.comment: quick: We rode some of the short slopes on the east side of Monarch Ramparts. Poked around other aspects which were wind hammered. Probed 150 cm at the top of the slope in the photo and found around 50 cm mid slope after loosing a ski to a rock and boot packing back up. Foot penetration to ground made for easy boot packing.

reports.title: Sunshine Meadows area
reports.comment: quick: Did an afternoon tour to Quartz/Larix area of Sunshine backcountry for some snow pit practice and a few turns. We found deeper-than-expected powder (up to 30 cm) on top of a mostly supportive midpack, making for good travel and skiing. Did shovel shear, column, and ECT tests at about 2350m on a W facing slope at 21 degrees with a depth of 80 to 100cm. Overall, we had a couple of easy (7+) r…

reports.title: Dinosaur Head
reports.comment: quick: In the Dinosaur Head the HS was 80cm.  The midpack was pretty weak and you would sink in facet holes occasionally while skinning.  Skiing was good but a bit sporty with unsupportive snow and more underbrush and small trees.  Snow was moist on the Healy pass trail below 1950m.  Strong NW winds today but at least broke up the 6-8mm surface Hoar present in the meadows yesterday.

reports.title: Grizzly Glades
reports.comment:
quick: Rode mellow terrain in Grizzly Glades 
10-15cm new snow skied well, no signs of instability. Some reverse loading from northerly winds. Slab overlying basal facets was more cohesive than it has been in recent weeks 

Performed compression test on SE aspect at 2370m. 29 degree slope angle. HS 110cm. 

CT6 sudden collapse 10-15cm down on new crust. 
CT14 sudden collapse ~45cm down on mid Dece…

reports.title: Healy Creek/ Centre Peak Tour
reports.comment: quick: We travelled from the Sunshine parking lot up towards Healy pass and then up the Y drainage to Centre Peak. Rode mellow east facing slopes down to Bourgeau meadows. Found a real mixed bag of snow, some windslab, some old tracks, some powder. Climbed back to the Ridgeline above Healy creek and bushwhacked our way into the low angle lower portion of Healy Pass Avy path #1. Found a mixed bag o…

reports.title: Wawa Ridge
reports.comment: quick: Wind slabs in isolated pockets today on Wawa. Cracks were propagating on low angles while skinning. Spent the day mostly below treeline where wind affect was minimal.

reports.title: Larix Lake area
reports.comment: quick: We did a few laps in the Southeast facing glades above Larix Lake today and found ok ski conditions. Supportive skinning with 20-40cm of ski pen in sheltered areas, quickly turning into 0-5cm in open areas above treeline. Even in sheltered areas, the surface snow was a upside down, with slabby/cakey snow on top and lower density snow below. No traditional signs of instability (whumphs and s…

reports.title: Avalanche control results - Sunshine Village access road
reports.comment: quick: 34 cm of snow has fallen since Feb 1 at Sunshine Village, plus strong SW winds in the last 48-hours. This has produced natural and explosive-triggered windslabs and deeper releases. These photos are the results observed today above the Sunshine Village access road.

reports.title: Healy Pass
reports.comment: quick: Great day of skiing. Snow was very good. On the tour up, we heard 4 natural avalanches. One of the four we could see through the trees. The mountains were very alive! This reaffirmed our decision to stay off slopes above 30 degrees.

reports.title: Exactly What You'd Expect
reports.comment: quick: We observed faint whumfing 2 or 3 times during the day, in the alpine.

reports.title: Wawa Bowl Skier Accidental
reports.comment: avalanche: Third skier on the slope triggered the avalanche which broke above them on the convexity. The windslab avalanche failed on 1mm facets above the P midpack. On investigation with a fracture profile; Extended column produced ECTP17 down 40cm on 1mm facets and a PST 37/100.

reports.title: Healey Pass Avalanche
reports.comment: quick: While skiing from Bourgeau Meadows over to Healey Pass we remote triggered a large avalanche off the ridge, location of avalanche 51.10434, -115.82293. The avalanche was remote triggered from approx. 100m away on a bench. We couldn’t see how large the avalanche was initially, but as we traversed through we could see that the crown was about 300 m wide, and up to 100cm deep. When we skied ou…

reports.title: Healy Pass
reports.comment: quick: 15cm new snow with range of 5-35cm. Snow quality was amazing. We stayed on low angle slopes; no avalanche terrain. Minor signs of instability on the uptrack. Nothing downhill. Nice to be out but would have loved more turns! Avalanche Risk is too high; expect it was High out there since there was more snow than predicted for the Considerable rating. / weather: Light wind. Little transport. /…

reports.title: Slide near Repeater Slopes, Wawa Ridge
reports.comment: quick: Size 2-2.5 avalanche on the SE side of Wawa Ridge from approximately 2410 to 2370m. I originally rated this as a 1.5 from the bottom, but after re-evaluation of the potential from the top view I have adjusted my rating to help keep others safe. The weak persistent layer is active. Deep slab separated down to the ground. After the slide we turned around and skied down the backdoor. Snow was …

reports.title: Woomf
reports.comment: quick: Whumpfing on skin track up east ridge. No movement

reports.title: Main Drain
reports.comment: quick: Extensive whumfing in the little larches on the east side and west side of the Wawa hump. Alpine was wind effected but in the trees skied good.  Flats were boggy and slow.

reports.title: Small slide under Sulfur gondola
reports.comment: avalanche: Triggered a small slide (Sz 0.5-1) underfoot while working underneath the Sulphur Mtn gondola. Wearing boots but no skis or snowshoes. Started as a point release/sluff and a small slab broke off down 50cm and ran ~30m on the basal facets. HS 70cm.The start zone was a small, steep, rocky feature that could have easily been avoided in hindsight.

reports.title: Healy Pass
reports.comment: quick: Skied a few short laps in the Healy pass area this morning. Observed some natural activity in the area from the last couple of days. A few size 1 slabs on the lee aspect of the Monarch Ramparts, these did not propagate or run far. Slabs on lee slopes on the Monarch's northeast aspect (can't remember what that line is called off the top of my head) and a north east facing bowl on Haiduk peak…

reports.title: Pilot Mountain deep slabs
reports.comment: quick: Multiple deep persistent slabs observed ok Pilot Mountain. Estimate these occurred on March 13 or 14.

reports.title: Twin Cairns Spring Laps
reports.comment: quick: Some small whumpfs, east steep face slid with the sun. North and North West and treed areas were fantastic.

reports.title: Sunshine Landing
reports.comment: quick: We had lots of settlement on our way up to Sunshine Landing. We stuck to slopes under 30’. All and all, it was a nice walk with minimal hazard.

reports.title: Twin Cairns skier remote
reports.comment: avalanche: Remotely triggered by public from ridge, no involvement.

reports.title: Wawa Ridge Full Profile
reports.comment: quick: Dry supportive snow on north aspect. Sun affected slopes became moist or had a breakable crust.

reports.title: Bourgeau Meadows
reports.comment: quick: No visible signs of new avalanches. Thought we heard two releases in the distance. / weather: Warm temperatures, some large flakes falling later in the day. Mix of cloud and intense sun. / snowpack: 5-10cm on top of obvious sun crust. Rode mellow slopes below 30cm with no reactivity. Some small slab movement of the new snow on the sun crust. Occaisional failure of sun crust on skinning.

reports.title: Massive Mountain
reports.comment: avalanche: This avalanche really caught us off guard.  It was triggered the third time we skied the run.  We intentionally avoided the crown area because it had an obvious windslab.  The crown was above our transition point.  One skier stopped half way down about dead center of the slide path in a treed area.  Two other party members were standing near the transition point watching the second skie…

reports.title: Spray River Falls - Ice climbing
reports.comment: quick: More new snow than expected from recent storms in the approach up the avalanche track just below the climb and on steep rocky terrain in the ALP. Cloudy early am today in this region. Within 30 minutes of solar exposure, several significant sluffs hit the first step of the climb. We got the message and promptly descended.

reports.title: Bearspirit - ice
reports.comment:
quick: **Approach in decent shape, used crampons from the creek to the ice but the ice step itself was easy.  A couple of windfallen trees cross the trail towards the climb. Not too hard to step over/under and between but somewhat large diameter and it would take a large saw to cut them.
**Curtain on the left side collapsed in the past so at this point in the season its unlikely to touch down and …

reports.title: Sunshine meadows, crust/corn season
reports.comment:
quick: It was hot the last two days with a light freeze over night.  In the sunshine Meadows the crust was supportive to skis but 10 cm boot pen. Relative cool cloudy day. When the sun came out at 3 pm the crust broke down quickly and sw slopes below 2300m became a bit punchy.

A new size 3  avalanche to ground toward Kootaney park on NW shallow alpine slope. And size 2 wet slab in eagle basin in …

reports.title: Bear Spirit - Ice climbing
reports.comment: quick: Note on approach - hazardous conditions at/above handline. Limited ice & snow, plenty of running water on slick slab. Rappeled it on the way out. Picked out dry ice on main flow. Some mixed routes have thin topouts.

reports.title: Sunshine Wawa N/ NE
reports.comment: quick: We skied some runs off Wawa ridge to the N and NE.  Conditions were wind pressed, windslab and wind scoured.  Breakable crust on solar and some good facet skiing in sheltered areas from the wind on polar.  The weather started out cold, overcast and windy and progressed to warmer -2 and broken by the end of the day.  Some drum like sounds were heard and another party off Twin Cairns area rep…

reports.title: Wawa Ridge
reports.comment: quick: Went up Wawa Ridge for a walk and to look at some low angle terrain. Lots of wind loading, firm wind blown snow. 110cm snow depth, started to dig a pit for my own educational purposes, and had sudden whoomphing and snow pack drop around us. Didn’t finish pit  and left area. It was in low angle approximate 22 degree slope. East facing. Below the top crust was all sugary snow.

reports.title: Borgeau right
reports.comment: avalanche: Saw what appeared to be a size 1.5-2 at 11am over borgeau right. Visible wind transport above both before and after the avalanche, likely the trigger. Skied up to wawa, similar transport visible all day, mind the overhead my friends!

reports.title: Avalanche Control Results Mt Bourgeau
reports.comment: quick: Parks Canada conducted helicopter avalanche control on Mt Bourgeau Thursday evening above the Sunshine Village Access road. While there was a great deal of natural activity in the area already from the previous cycle, 4 of 6 explosives produced very good results on the higher targets. While there were some good propagations in the start zones, as a result of cooling since the storm, these a…

reports.title: Healy 123, lost peak and centre peak
reports.comment:
quick: Still significant whumpfing on mostly sheltered and polar aspects. 
Reactive wind slabs forming along the Lee side in the alpine.
Sun crust all the way to our high point 2550m 1-3”.
Good skiing on the polar aspects.
Multiple Late afternoon Size 1 Loose wet avalanche’s in the “y” drainage.

reports.title: Birdwood traverse
reports.comment:
quick: Lots of small size 1 releases of storm slabs.

The one pictured seemed let go then stepped down through the sun-crust.

1 -2cm sun-crust on solar aspect with 1-5 cm of facets over solid wind hammered surface

reports.title: Quartz Hill
reports.comment: quick: Good freeze and travel conditions in the Alpine and treeline. A couple cm of new snow made for some soft skiing in the morning. Crusts broke down quickly below tree line. The snow was punchy on steep SE wind protected aspect at 12:15 at 2250m off the whaleback. A few new wet loose/wet slab avalanches to size 1.5  but thin cirrus clouds prevented it from getting hot today. On Monday serval d…

reports.title: SSV area
reports.comment:
quick: Not that you need a MIN as there’s a SPAW and a red brick. But word from confessions of a ski bum came to mind when he previously said he saw skied out runs rip in the past. Of note at SSV and area:

- Mother in law off Goats eye ripped out size 2 yesterday (a resort ski run in trees)
- Howard Douglas / Eagle basin ripped again this time scrubbing to ground from the top
- Wheelers (in Wild …
